extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task requiring broad discourse context. LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages where human subjects are able to guess the last word if exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. In Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 1525–1534.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were extracted from the Book Corpus and filtered automatically using four language models to remove cases easily guessable from local context. A sample of the remaining passages was evaluated by human subjects through CrowdFlower in three steps: two subjects sequentially guessed the target word given the broad context, and up to ten subjects attempted to guess it given only the target sentence. Passages were included only if both broad-context subjects guessed the target word correctly and no local-context subject could guess it.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), consisting of unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list, leaving 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Novels were randomly partitioned into disjoint training (2,662 novels, >200M words) and development+testing sets. Passages were extracted with a context of at least 50 tokens (average 4.6 sentences) plus a target sentence. Automated filtering excluded any passage where the target word had a probability >= 0.00175 according to any of four language models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdsourcing via CrowdFlower in three sequential steps: 1) one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if correct, 2) a second subject guessed based on the whole passage; if also correct, 3) additional subjects (up to 10, each allowed 3 guesses) tried guessing the target word based only on the target sentence. If no subject in step 3 guessed correctly, the passage was added to the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Strict hit-or-miss criteria were enforced: two consecutive subjects had to provide the exact target word given the full passage, while none of up to ten subjects (with 3 guesses each) could provide it based on the target sentence alone. Plausible synonyms were not included as valid alternatives due to practical and methodological challenges in evaluating non-exact substitutions at scale.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between 3 and 12 human subjects (2 broad-context subjects and up to 10 target-sentence-only subjects)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: English speakers; subjects were paid $0.22 per page in steps 1 and 2 (10 passages per page) and $0.15 per page in step 3 (20 sentences per page)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A pre-trained recurrent neural network (Mikolov et al., 2011), and three models trained on the Book Corpus (a standard 4-gram model, an RNN, and a feed-forward model) used to filter out easy passages; lemmatizer.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are heavily over-represented (48% of target words) compared to the input distribution; more than 80% of passages contain the target word or its lemma in the context; direct quoted speech occurs significantly more often (71%) than in the broader input sample (61%). Verbs (7.7%), adjectives, and adverbs are relatively rare.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Requires strict exact-word matching, ignoring valid synonymous continuations. Standard language models fail by construction because passages predictable by local language models were filtered out. Skewed part-of-speech distribution with an overabundance of proper nouns and an underrepresentation of verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and validation benchmark for measuring broad discourse context understanding in language models and NLP systems; development set can be used for fine-tuning.
